title: Data Hypothesis
tag: Hypothesis 1 of 2 · for you to pass or correct
h1: The data: what is wrong with it, and what to build instead
lead: Nothing was built, collected or downloaded for this. It is the argued plan for the data that the model will be trained and tested on. The second hypothesis, for the model, follows.
reached: An honest label first: this was not a graph of thoughts. Five whole designs were scored once and then merged once, by me, in a single pass.
steps: Seven tests and nine vetoes, written before any rival design existed.
Four separate runs from different starting points, blind to each other, plus my own earlier draft.
35 verdicts, each with its learning entries. Five facts the runs reported were checked in our code: all hold.
Each part taken from the design where it is strongest. 15 decisions.
Every one of the 43 data entries held against the result. After that I re-read it twice myself; that changed details only.

designs.name: Questions
designs.verdict: Strongest on the questions: texts sorted by when they were written, a change question with a real moment of asking, error sources in tiers.

designs.name: Population
designs.start: Started from which repositories the model must work on
designs.verdict: Strongest on the sample and on time: the only list that is complete for what it defines, copies treated as one project, a cut-off date.

designs.name: Code
designs.start: Started from the code as it stands
designs.verdict: Strongest on content and on kinds of link: every file parsed, every failed link kept with its reason, a test for repositories with little history.

designs.name: Repair
designs.start: Started from keeping what we have
designs.verdict: Argued for keeping and still ended at rebuilding three parts. Alone had: errors from failing checks, a cut per question, a leak test that rebuilds from a cut copy.

designs.name: First draft
designs.verdict: Removed. Matched or beaten on every test by three of the four others. Two of its parts were struck by a veto.

limits: The merge was one pass by one mind. No rival merge was made, the merged design was not scored by the same recorded steps as the five designs, and where the designs disagreed I chose in that pass or put the point off. A real graph of thoughts would have worked on exactly those points. That is the weak spot of this hypothesis.

The four runs were given the yardstick, which already demands a lossless store, a designed sample and time-correct inputs. That all five designs agree on those points repeats the yardstick; it is not independent proof. The runs earned their place by what they added beyond it.

Hiding which design was which from the judge would have hidden nothing: the starting points show in the text and one design is my own. So every verdict is recorded with the entries it rests on and can be checked.
This cannot prove the design right. It gives the best-argued one and names the counts that are still needed.
